Title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus/First Part/Proof 3

Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Real Function|real function]] which is [[Definition:Continuous on Interval|continuous]] on the [[Definition:Closed Real Interval|closed interval]] $\closedint a b$.

Let $F$ be a [[Definition:Real Function|real function]] which is defined on $\closedint a b$ by:
:$\ds \map F x = \int_a^x \map f t \rd t$

Then $F$ is a [[Definition:Primitive (Calculus)|primitive]] of $f$ on $\closedint a b$.
